journey.definition: an act of traveling from one place to another; a trip.
examples: The journey began at dawn.

jazz.definition: a music genre characterized by improvisation and swing.
examples: The concert featured classic jazz.

juice.definition: a liquid drink made from fruit or vegetables.
examples: She drinks apple juice at lunch.
Her joyful smile brightened the room.
They were joyous when they won.
It was a joyous day for the family.

judgment.definition: an opinion or decision made after thinking about something carefully
examples: Her judgment helped the team choose the safest option.
The judge’s judgment was final.

judgment.definition: the ability to make sensible decisions
examples: Using good judgment is important in emergencies.
He has poor judgment when he drives at night.

jostle.definition: to push or bump into someone because of crowding or movement
examples: People jostled in the crowd as the train arrived.
She jostled past the other passengers.
He felt jittery after too much coffee.
The jittery driver slowed down suddenly.

juror.definition: a member of a jury who listens to a case and helps decide the verdict
examples: One juror asked for clarification of the evidence.
The jurors reached a decision after two days.

jurist.definition: a person who studies or practices law
examples: A jurist wrote the legal opinion for the court.
The jurist explained the new legislation.

judicious.definition: showing good judgment; wise and careful
examples: It was a judicious decision to wait before responding.
She made a judicious choice.

jurisdiction.definition: the legal authority to make decisions and enforce laws in a specific area
examples: The case fell under federal jurisdiction.
The court lacked jurisdiction to try the matter.

jurisprudence.definition: the study of law and legal principles
examples: Her research is in jurisprudence.
Jurisprudence helps explain how laws are interpreted.

juris.definition: related to law; used as part of legal words (not commonly used alone)
examples: Juris is usually part of terms like jurisprudence.

juristic.definition: relating to law or legal reasoning
examples: The juristic analysis focused on contract interpretation.
He published juristic commentary.

journalist.definition: a person who collects information and writes or reports news
examples: The journalist interviewed the mayor.
He worked as a journalist for the local paper.

jingle.definition: a short bright sound, especially the ringing of small bells
examples: She heard a jingle as the keys moved in the bowl.
The store’s sign made a soft jingle when someone walked by.

jingle.definition: a short catchy tune or set of words used for advertising
examples: That jingle gets stuck in my head every time the ad plays.
The company’s jingle helped the product become well known.

jingle.definition: to make a short bright ringing sound
examples: The bracelets jingle when she walks.
Coins jingle in his pocket as he searches for change.

jangle.definition: to make a repeated sharp ringing sound
examples: The keys jangled in her pocket.
I heard a jangle as the chain moved.

jangle.definition: a sharp ringing noise, often repeated
examples: There was a jangle of metal from the gate.
The jangle made her look up.

jess.definition: a strap or leather band, used to attach a falcon to something or to control it in falconry
examples: The trainer fitted the jess to the bird.
A jess keeps the falcon under control.

jeer.definition: to laugh or shout in an insulting way to show contempt
examples: The crowd jeered when he made that mistake.
They jeered at the performer.
There were jeers from the back row.
The jeer made her turn around.

justify.definition: to give a good reason or proof for an action or belief
examples: Can you justify your decision?
She justified the expense with receipts.

justify.definition: to align text so that the edges of lines look even
examples: The document is set to justify the paragraphs.

journal.definition: a newspaper or magazine, especially one focused on business, academic work, or professional topics
examples: I read a journal about computer science.
The journal published the research results.

journal.definition: a book where you write your daily thoughts or experiences
examples: She kept a journal during her travels.
He wrote in his journal every night.

journal.definition: to write notes or records in a journal
examples: She journals her progress weekly.
He journals about his day and his feelings.

judge.definition: a person who has authority to decide cases in a court of law
examples: The judge delivered the sentence in court.
A judge reviewed the evidence.

judge.definition: a person who decides the winners in a competition
examples: The judges will score each performance.
She served as a judge for the contest.

judge.definition: to decide or form an opinion after considering information
examples: It is hard to judge his skill from one game.
She judged the situation carefully.

jagged.definition: rough and uneven, with sharp points or edges
examples: The rock has jagged edges.
He cut his hand on a jagged piece of metal.
